# Hive

> Hive is a portable guidance layer for deliberate work with coding agents. It supplies shared rules, activity skills, and specialist role definitions, plus a Go manager that installs them into the native locations of Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Pi, OpenCode V2, Cursor CLI, and Antigravity. Each host keeps its own model loop, authentication, tools, permissions, and history. Building the manager from source requires Go 1.27.4 or later.

Distributable content lives in `content/` and `integrations/`; the manager is in `tooling/`. `_support/`, `tests/`, and the root `AGENTS.md` are maintainer material for this repository and are not installed; `site/` is the documentation site for people and is not installed either. Links are relative to the repository root.

## Docs

- [Documentation site](https://hive.tricell.tech/): getting started, a skills catalog with flow guides, a flows overview, inspiration projects, and a changelog rendered from CHANGELOG.md; each flow page links to its skill
- [README](README.md): overview, installation (one-line, release package, or source), hosts, update, recovery, and uninstall. One-line install: `curl -fsSL https://hive.tricell.tech/install.sh | sh`; append `-s -- --dry-run --hosts <hosts>` to preview without changing any host, which needs no terminal; a real installation needs a terminal. `hive update` installs a compatible published release (0.9.0 or newer), after installations of 0.8.0 or earlier run the 0.9.0-or-newer installer once; `hive update --source DIR` remains the committed-source route
- [One-line installer script](get-hive.sh): what the one-line command downloads and runs
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): release history, starting with 0.1.0
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): local test suite, viewer frontend development (Node >=24 and pnpm 12.8.1), checked-in bundle freshness, conventions, and language rules
- [Security](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately
- [Installer contract](_support/docs/architecture/installer.md): package checks, migration, and interrupted-install recovery
- [Deployment manager](_support/docs/architecture/deployment-manager.md): manager commands, plans, scopes, ownership, and recovery
- `hive voice list|set|off`: list the voices, select one, or turn it off (see the manager contract above)
- `hive project set`: edit the `## Hive` section of a repository's `AGENTS.md` after confirmation; the section holds facts, and `hive doctor` exits non-zero on a blocking finding in it
- `hive releases`: list the retained release snapshots
- [Agent delivery](_support/docs/architecture/agent-delivery.md): canonical roles, native profiles, and per-host delegation limits

## Guidance

The global core retains essential boundaries and explicit read conditions for
canonical procedures. Reporting is read under the conditions
`content/guidance/global.md` states, not before every reply; other procedures
are selected by their stated conditions, not all preloaded. A packaged
file, its discovery, its delivery into context and compliance are separate facts.
Source-byte unions are not actual tokens or evidence of small-model reliability.

- [Shared guidance](content/guidance/global.md): authorization, preservation, secrets, evidence, artifact placement, questions and routes between flows, project settings, persistent memory and scope changes, installed into each host
- [flow-research status mode](content/skills/flow-research/references/status.md): report the backlog and unfinished work, read-only, and recommend what to take next
- [flow-research](content/skills/flow-research/SKILL.md): entry for every request to do work: settle what the user needs, then answer, continue into build, or go to plan only when the how has a decision for the user; also investigates a question, assesses a chosen ticket or audits a codebase for what to improve, ending analyses at the findings
- [flow-figma-design](content/skills/flow-figma-design/SKILL.md): optional stage between research and plan: draw one example of a new or recomposed screen as frames in the project's Figma file, following the app's existing screens (alternatives only for a screen the user names), have the completed set reviewed, then ask once to approve or correct it, with applicable mobile frames ready, and record the approved examples the plan, build and verification compare against, with a rule card beside each frame for its business rules, which the work also writes to its ticket when the example is approved, when the build starts and at the close; corrections return only affected screens for approval, while proposed business rules remain separate decisions
- [flow-plan](content/skills/flow-plan/SKILL.md): settle the how: present approaches, resolve decisions and define contracts, tasks, and acceptance criteria
- [flow-build](content/skills/flow-build/SKILL.md): implement authorized work and hand over a built candidate
- [flow-verify](content/skills/flow-verify/SKILL.md): verify the candidate at the level the session's answers and the request set, then integrate it, with a security review only when the user asks
- [flow-close](content/skills/flow-close/SKILL.md): move the ticket, write the work's business rules to it and report at integration, end with a close footer, and clean up the work's resources and the merged branches and clean worktrees of each repository it touched on the user's reply, commit the change folder at a pause where the specs repository allows it, honoring a `Completion` key's later completion point
- [flow-deploy](content/skills/flow-deploy/SKILL.md): promote an integrated candidate through the declared environments and verify what is served, moving tickets to the final state a `Completion` key names
- [git-workflow](content/skills/git-workflow/SKILL.md): prepare authorized Git delivery while preserving unrelated work
- [hive-ui-criteria](content/skills/hive-ui-criteria/SKILL.md): detect the project's component library, installed version and customization layer, keep them in a verified `DESIGN.md`, and give design, build and review work measurable UI criteria below the project's own design system
- [flow-verify walkthrough](content/skills/flow-verify/references/walkthrough.md): publish UI captures and their iteration to the viewer, and present a built interface for validation
- [flow-report](content/skills/flow-report/SKILL.md): a designed HTML report, comparison, explainer or deck
- [flow-report docs-site mode](content/skills/flow-report/references/docs-site.md): scaffold, extend or audit a documentation site
- [harness-audit](content/skills/harness-audit/SKILL.md): audit agent instructions, skills and role definitions, ask the decisions the findings need, and apply the accepted outcomes, including a repository's `## Hive` section
- [harness-audit local instructions mode](content/skills/harness-audit/references/local-instructions.md): create or prune the untracked HIVE.local.md of a project and the machine file (~/.config/hive/HIVE.local.md) from what already worked on this machine, after asking which facts to keep
- [flow-research security advisory mode](content/skills/flow-research/references/security-advisory.md): check whether a published advisory affects a set of repositories, without changing them
- [test-audit](content/skills/test-audit/SKILL.md): prune one area's duplicate or implementation-coupled tests to one owner per contract, proven by an independent review and targeted mutations
- [flow-close support maintenance](content/skills/flow-close/references/support-maintenance.md): organize support artifacts and retained evidence
- [unattended-delegation](content/skills/unattended-delegation/SKILL.md): coordinate delegated work with a bounded objective and expiry
- [harness-audit Engram workspace mode](content/skills/harness-audit/references/engram-workspace.md): establish one Engram identity for a declared workspace, only when asked
- [Role profiles](integrations/agent-profiles.json): default model and effort per role and host
- [Instruction resources](_support/docs/architecture/instruction-resources.md): canonical procedure homes, resolution, payload validation and declared reading-footprint scenarios
- [Optional OpenCode context loader](_support/docs/architecture/deployment-manager.md#optional-opencode-context-loader): delivered inactive at user scope as `<OpenCodeHome>/hive/context-loader/{index.js,context-loader.json}`, outside `plugins/`, with no `package.json`; activate only the installed `hive/context-loader` directory, not the editorial template. It supplies two fixed-role snapshots without runtime reference/metadata reads; refresh requires manager regeneration and plugin reload, not a live Markdown edit. Metadata schema 2 records role/resource/digest provenance, not cryptographic authentication. Deactivation/removal preserves user configuration. Package manifest v2 is separate from metadata schema 2; v1 packages remain readable by the current manager

## Optional

- [Local viewer](README.md#review-ui-walkthroughs-in-one-place): shared-work timeline of UI captures with their iteration, immutable evidence and current canonical references; agents publish only captures with `hive view work capture`, while stage, task, evidence and Markdown publication stay as advanced operations (`hive view work contract`, `hive view contract`); the browser's management actions also from the CLI (`hive view work rename|archive|restore|pin|unpin|recover|delete`); automatic visibility archival after closure, manual content retention, capture publication (`work capture`, closed with `work close`, queued while the viewer is stopped), host-observed session activity and native tasks through `hive hook` registered per host at user-scope install (Codex needs approval in `/hooks`), and a coordinated timeline revision 3 update within protocol 3
- [Viewer manual](site/src/content/docs/viewer.md): read tasks, stage activity, galleries, document revisions, canonical references and CI waits; manage the local work library.
- [Viewer frontend](tooling/viewer/frontend/README.md): standalone development package, real API by default, explicit development preview, same-tab navigation persistence, bundle contract and checks
- [Third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): Go and embedded frontend license notices

- [Repository structure](_support/docs/architecture/repository-and-distribution.md): layout, ownership, and managed instruction blocks
- [Optional tool dependencies](_support/docs/architecture/tool-dependencies.md): Engram, Context7, pi-subagents (whose `extensions/subagent/config.json` gets `"toolActivation": "eager"` when the key is missing, with `hive plan remove`), agent-browser, the Codex question card (`codex-question-card`), the Codex wait floor (`codex-wait-floor`, which writes `min_wait_timeout_ms` and `default_wait_timeout_ms` under `[features.multi_agent_v2]` in Codex's `config.toml`, with a backup and `hive plan remove`), and CodeGraph
- [Harness engineering research](_support/docs/harness-engineering/README.md): research sources and the measurement standard
- [Model support floor](_support/docs/harness-engineering/model-floor.md): the models the guidance is written for (role-profile models) and the floor candidates, Haiku and flash-class included, whose observed failures count toward a correction
- [History and provenance](_support/docs/history/history-and-provenance.md): how the project evolved
- [Requirements and change records](_support/openspec/): versioned requirements and planned changes
- [Tests](tests/): content checks, fixtures, and evaluation tooling
